security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's mpmpdeleg CSR write handler accepts a pmpnum value that is less than or equal to the index of any locked PMP entry (pmpcfg[i].L == 1), instead of ignoring the write and retaining the prior pmpnum value as mandated by the WARL constraint. This allows M-mode software (or a buggy M-mode firmware running on QEMU) to unintentionally delegate locked M-mode PMP regions into SPMP control, where S-mode can subsequently reconfigure spmpcfg/spmpaddr to alter permissions on memory regions that M-mode intended to permanently lock.
security_spec.summary: Unenforced WARL constraint on mpmpdeleg.pmpnum allows S-mode to reconfigure M-mode-locked PMP regions via SPMP delegation bypass

findings.finding: The mpmpdeleg CSR and pmpnum field are not implemented in this QEMU codebase. The mseccfg CSR write handler only processes Smepmp fields (MML, MMWP, RLB, PMM, MLPE); there is no SSPMP bit, no pmpnum WARL logic, and no PMP-to-SPMP delegation mechanism. The Sspmp extension is entirely absent.
